{
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "summary_length",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.35,
      "source_groundedness": 0.95,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Raw character length of the summary; a generic surface metric with weak analytical leverage for explaining low scores, but values are directly and correctly derivable from the text."
    },
    {
      "name": "text_length",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.4,
      "source_groundedness": 0.95,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Review text length is a plausible but weak generic feature. Values match source text (e.g. taffy review = 140). Low leverage for THIS query as a bare length count."
    },
    {
      "name": "has_negative_words",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.6,
      "source_groundedness": 0.6,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "A negative-lexicon flag is relevant to explaining low scores. However groundedness is questionable: the 'Not as Advertised' complaint row is flagged 0, showing the lexicon misses clear negativity, undermining reliability of the values."
    },
    {
      "name": "has_positive_words",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.55,
      "source_groundedness": 0.85,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Positive-word flag gives a sentiment axis useful for contrasting with low scores. Sampled values look sound (positive reviews flagged 1, the complaint flagged 0)."
    },
    {
      "name": "helpfulness_ratio",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.7,
      "source_groundedness": 0.95,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Directly computed from existing numerator/denominator columns; a genuinely useful ratio to correlate with score. Slightly redundant with originals but adds a normalized axis."
    },
    {
      "name": "has_complaint_markers",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.7,
      "source_groundedness": 0.55,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Complaint markers directly target the query. But groundedness is weak: the clearly positive 'Delight'/'heaven' review is flagged 1, a false positive that contradicts the source, indicating a noisy marker rule."
    },
    {
      "name": "uppercase_ratio",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.4,
      "source_groundedness": 0.9,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Uppercase ratio can proxy shouting/emphasis, mildly relevant to negative reviews, but a weak generic surface feature. Values are computable from text."
    },
    {
      "name": "exclamation_count",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.4,
      "source_groundedness": 0.95,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Punctuation count is a generic feature with modest leverage for score explanation; values are trivially derivable and match samples (all 0 here)."
    },
    {
      "name": "question_count",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.35,
      "source_groundedness": 0.95,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Question-mark count is near-constant (mostly 0) and offers little analytical leverage, though values are correctly derived."
    },
    {
      "name": "is_low_score",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.5,
      "source_groundedness": 0.6,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "As the target label this is useful for framing the analysis, but it is essentially a restatement of the existing Score column. Grounding is shaky: the 'Cough Medicine' row (medicinal but not clearly a rating) is flagged low_score=1 while source gives no explicit rating cue, suggesting derivation from Score which is fine—but the taffy/positive rows labeled 0 are consistent."
    }
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.55,
  "source_groundedness": 0.78,
  "rationale": "The set mixes genuinely relevant axes (helpfulness_ratio, sentiment/complaint flags, the low-score label) with several generic surface metrics (summary_length, text_length, uppercase_ratio, exclamation_count, question_count) that add limited leverage for explaining low scores. Most values are soundly derivable from the source text, but the lexicon/marker-based flags show observable misfires in the samples—'Not as Advertised' not flagged negative and the positive 'Delight' review flagged as a complaint—lowering confidence in groundedness for those columns."
}
